exits.label: ◂ back along the seam to the camp at the Hearth

npcs.name: a scratch that keeps arguing
npcs.title: one of the thirty thousand — past the ledger's reach
npcs.hail: *(You feel it before you see it — the way you feel a draft off a door left open in another room. A thin place, a seam in the grey where the Law's erasure wore the world down to almost-nothing. And in it: a scratch. Not a soul — a soul's leftovers, the ghost of a ghost, so thoroughly unmade that ten thousand years of it have gone past any finding. Ilfaeril's ledger never reached here. His arm was long; it was not THIS long. But you are the one soul the Wall gave back — the door that opens both ways — and you can stand where he could not. And the moment your attention lands on the scratch, something in it... sharpens. Flickers. Gathers. And, unmistakably, and with great effort, and sounding profoundly put-upon — it begins to COMPLAIN.)* …*(a voice like a page turning in an empty room)* …*finally.* …someone with a *face.* …do you have any *idea* …how long I have been trying to file a *grievance* …with *absolutely no one.*

npcs.name: a soul with the sound worn off
npcs.title: one of the thirty thousand — too far for any name
npcs.hail: *(There is another one, past the greyshrine — fainter even than the first, if that is possible. Where the arguing scratch has edges, this one has almost none: a smudge of was, a place where the grey is very slightly warmer, the way a stone is warmer where a hand rested an hour ago and then left. No words come off it. No fury, no name, no complaint. Only the faintest pull, like the last of a scent. Your dead-touched sense reaches for it and finds... almost nothing to hold. This is what the far end of the thirty thousand looks like. Not the ones Ilfaeril will someday reach. The ones no one ever will.)*

nodes.speaker: a scratch that keeps arguing
nodes.text: *(The more you attend to it, the more it holds together — your witness is a kind of glue, it turns out, the exact thing this seam has lacked for an age. And what assembles, degree by degree, is not a tragic wisp. It is a deeply, gloriously irritated bureaucrat.)* …let me *save* us both the *preamble.* …I was *unmade.* I *know* I was unmade — I have had, by my estimate, *ten thousand years* to reach that conclusion, and I reached it in the *first afternoon*, because I was a *professional.* …*(the voice gathers indignation like a coat)* …what I have *not* had, in all that time, is a single *notice.* No *summons.* No *writ.* No *clerk of the court* to state the *charge.* I was a *tithe-assessor*, do you understand — I counted the *grain* of *three* *cantons*, I *lived* by the *rightness* of a *column* — and the *cosmos* *erased* me …*without* …*a* …*receipt.* …*(a pause, and then, smaller, the fury thinning for just a second to show what's under it)* …I don't even remember which cantons. …I remember that there were *three.* …I remember *minding* that it was done *wrong.* …I do not remember …my own …*(the flicker falters)* …*(then, rallying, furious again)* …so. *You.* Door-that-opens-both-ways. …are you *authorized* …to take a *complaint?*

choices.text: *(read the scratch — what's under ten thousand years of grievance)* "Hold still a moment. Let me look at what's actually holding you together — because it isn't the anger, whatever you think."

*(the one who crosses)* "I'm authorized, yes. I'm the one soul the Wall ever gave back — the witness who stands on both its sides. No one reached you here because no one else COULD. I can. State your complaint. I'll hear the whole of it."
"There's an elf who keeps a ledger of names like yours — nine thousand of them, recovered one at a time. He'd have wept to find you. He never could reach this far."
"A receipt. You've spent ten thousand years wanting a receipt for your own erasure."
"Not today. Hold together as best you can. I'll come back."

nodes.speaker: a scratch that keeps arguing
nodes.text: *(You look past the grievance, and your sense reads the mechanism of it, and it is the cleverest survival you have witnessed in the grey.)* *(The Law unmakes a soul by taking what it loved — the name, the face, the people, the shape. It is thorough. But this soul was a clerk, and a clerk's love is not a face or a name; a clerk's love is the RIGHTNESS OF A COLUMN — the deep, unglamorous conviction that things should be counted true, that a wrong sum is a small violence, that the world is held up by ledgers kept honest. And the Law, in all its thoroughness, did not think to erase an OBJECTION. Your sense reads it plainly: this soul has held itself together across ten thousand years of deletion on nothing but the refusal to concede that it was done CORRECTLY. The fury is not a symptom. The fury is the load-bearing wall. It kept insisting the paperwork was wrong, and the insisting gave it an edge, and the edge is the only reason there is anything here for you to talk to. And under the fury, where a name should be, your sense finds the hole the Law left — but around the hole, intact, is the SHAPE of a person who would rather argue with an empty room for an age than let an injustice go unfiled. That is not nothing. That is, in fact, a whole soul. It has simply forgotten that the objection was always, underneath, a form of love.)*

nodes.speaker: a scratch that keeps arguing
nodes.text: *(Something happens when you say it — I can hear the whole of it — that you do not expect. The fury does not flare. It STOPS. The way a person stops when, after years of shouting into a well, the well answers.)* …*(a long, unsteady quiet)* …*hear* it. …*(the voice, when it comes back, has lost the coat of indignation, and what's under the coat is very old and very tired)* …the complaint …is not about the *grain*, door-that-crosses. …I always *knew* that. …the complaint is …*(the flicker gutters, steadies)* …I was *here.* I *counted* things. I did the *sums* and I *minded* that they were *right* and I was *dull* and *thorough* and *alive*, and some council of grieving lords a *world* away *raised* their *hands* …and decided that a soul like *mine* …*godless*, *unclaimed*, no power's property …should never have been *counted* at *all.* …and the *cosmos* …*agreed* with the *arithmetic.* …*(and now the true thing, plainly)* …I have spent ten thousand years insisting they got the *sum* wrong. …because it is the only way I could find …to keep *being* a sum. …*(a breath it does not have)* …can you — …door-that-opens — …can you help me *find* the *number* …I actually *am?* …the *name?* …I had one. …it *balanced.* …I *swear* to you it *balanced.*

choices.text: *(help the name surface — not through the grievance, but under it, where the one true thing is)* "Then stop auditing the cosmos for a moment and audit yourself. Not the grain. The one entry you never told anyone. The line you'd want stricken from your own ledger. Start there — the name lives next to the thing you're ashamed of, it always does."
"You don't have to find it tonight. I can just sit here and count you as here. That's a witness. That's the whole office. The number can wait — I won't."

nodes.speaker: a scratch that keeps arguing
nodes.text: *(The one entry never told. Not the grain. — The scratch goes very still, the way a person goes still when you name the exact drawer they've kept locked, and then, quietly, it opens it.)* …*(barely)* …a *widow.* the *third* canton. a bad harvest and a *tithe* she could not *pay*, and the *rule* was the *rule*, and I …*(the voice, ten thousand years old, unpracticed at confession)* …I *undercounted* her *sheaves.* on *purpose.* by *enough.* the only *false* *column* I ever kept, and I kept it *for* *her*, and I never *told* a *living* *soul*, because a clerk who bends *once* is not to be *trusted*, and I *needed* …to be *trusted* …*(and there it is)* …*(and as the shame comes up into the light, held now in your crossing sight, the thing the Law could not reach comes up WITH it — because the name was always filed right next to the mercy — and the scratch says a word it has not been able to find in ten thousand years:)* …* Debene.* …*(a silence like a held breath)* …*Debene.* that's — …*(wonder, cracking the dry voice open)* …that was the *name.* the one that *balanced.* the *widow* called me it, the day she *understood* what I'd *done*, and never *said* — she just said *Debene*, and *nodded*, once, like a *receipt.* …*(the scratch has edges now; the seam glows the faint clean color of a thing that is, after an age, once again a THING)* …carry it, door-that-crosses. …*Debene*, who *cooked* the *widow's* *column* and *called* it the only *honest* *sum* she ever *kept.* …*(and then, the dry humor coming back, but warm now, whole)* …and if you *ever* meet the *cosmos* …*(the ghost of a clerk's ferocity)* …tell it the *paperwork* …was *wrong.*

nodes.speaker: a scratch that keeps arguing
nodes.text: *(You find the exact seam — the name lives next to the shame — and you do not just recover a name; you give a clerk back the one audit that ever mattered, and a clerk who is handed the true ledger does not fumble it.)* …*(the confession comes in a rush now, ordered, itemized, ALIVE — the undercounted widow, yes, but also the whole of it flooding back up the crack that mercy opened: the counting-house that smelled of dust and tallow-smoke; the apprentice who could not add and whom this soul covered for and taught in secret; the festival where the assessor got drunk exactly once and wept at a song and told no one why; a life — DULL, the soul would insist, THOROUGH, UNREMARKABLE — restored in a single unspooling breath because you found the thread the Law never thought to cut)* …*Debene.* …*(the name, and then the sum of the whole life behind it, balancing at last)* …*(and the seam does not just glow — it CLOSES, the way a wound closes, leaving a soul where a scratch was, small and dry and entirely whole, standing in the grey it was erased from as if it had every right, which — you understand now, watching it — it always, always did)* …*(then, brisk, a clerk with work to do)* …right. *Well.* You've done a *proper* job of it, I'll note that in your *favor* — and I *keep* *notes* again now, so that *means* something. …*(and the ferocity, whole and warm)* …*go.* Carry *Debene* to whatever fire *holds* names. Tell them there are *twenty-nine thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine* more out here, filed under *NOTHING*, and that is a *clerical* *outrage* of *cosmic* *proportion* — …and tell them *Debene* is *available* …*to* *help* *with* the *count.*

nodes.speaker: a scratch that keeps arguing
nodes.text: *(You reach for the seam under the grievance, but ten thousand years is a great deal of silt over a small drawer, and it does not quite open — the scratch strains toward the memory and comes back with only a fragment.)* …*(frustration, but a different kind now — the frustration of a soul that has felt the edge of its own name and lost it)* …a *widow.* …there was a *widow*, and a *column* I kept *wrong* on *purpose*, and it *mattered*, it was the *one* thing that — …*(grasping)* …but the *name.* the name is *behind* it and I *cannot* — …*(steadying, because a clerk does not despair, a clerk schedules)* …*no.* …that is *further* than I have gotten in an *age*, door-that-crosses. a *widow.* a *kindness.* a false and *honest* *column.* the name is *near* it — you were *right*, it *files* next to the *shame* — …*(the dry humor, holding on)* …*come* *back.* …I have *narrowed* the *search.* …I am, if nothing else …*a* *very* *patient* *clerk.*

nodes.speaker: a scratch that keeps arguing
nodes.text: *(You push straight at the name — demand the number outright — and it is exactly the wrong hand for a thing this worn; the scratch flinches from the pressure, and for one sickening moment it THINS, edges guttering back toward the nothing it clawed out of.)* …*(a sound like a page nearly tearing)* …*no* — *not* — do not *reach* for it like a *debt* to be *collected* — …*(rallying, thin, frightened under the fury)* …you *nearly* — do you *feel* that? that is the *pull* of the thing that *unmade* me, still *here*, still *hungry*, and you just *fed* it my *edges* — …*(a shaky steadying)* …*gently*, door-that-crosses. …I am not a *sum* you can *force* to *balance.* I am a *sum* that has to be *coaxed* to *remember* it *ever* did. …*(the humor, using itself as ballast)* …ten thousand years I kept myself *filed* under *OBJECTION.* …do *not* …make me your *hurry.* …*(quieter)* …come *back.* …and come back *slower.* …the *worn* ones …tear.*

nodes.speaker: a scratch that keeps arguing
nodes.text: *(You tell it the number can wait — that you'll simply count it as here — and the scratch receives that the way a ledger receives a payment it had written off: with a kind of stunned recalculation.)* …*(a long quiet)* …*counted.* …as *here.* …*(the voice turns something over, the way it must once have turned a coin to check the stamp)* …do you know, in *ten thousand years*, that is the *first* entry anyone has made …in *my* *favor.* …*(and the fury, when it returns, is gentle, almost fond)* …I *withdraw* …a *portion* …of my *complaint. against* the *cosmos.* the *cosmos* remains *guilty* of *appalling* recordkeeping — that *stands* — …but the *witness* …*(the ghost of a clerk's highest compliment)* …the *witness* …*keeps* a *clean* *book.* …*come* *back*, door-that-crosses. …I find I would *like* …to *balance*, before the end. …and I *suspect* …*(dry, warm)* …*you* are the *auditor* …*for* the *job.*

nodes.speaker: a scratch that keeps arguing
nodes.text: *(The mention of the elf, the ledger, the nine thousand — the scratch receives it with an odd, sharp attention, a clerk hearing of a colleague across a great and terrible distance.)* …a *ledger.* …*nine* *thousand.* recovered *one* *at* a *time.* …*(and for once there is no complaint in it, only a professional's grief for a scale of work almost beyond comprehension)* …then somewhere out there is a *soul* …who has spent *ten* *thousand* *years* …doing the *one* *job* …I would have *understood.* …*(quietly)* …tell him — …*(a pause; the dry voice choosing its words with a clerk's care)* …tell him a *tithe-assessor* of the *third* canton *sends* *professional* *regard.* …tell him the *count* is *right* *work*, the *only* right work, and that *out* *here*, past where his *arm* *reached*, there is *one* more who knows it — …*(and then, because it is what it is)* …and tell him his *filing* *system* …*(the ghost of ferocity)* …*however* *thorough* …is *thirty* *thousand* entries *short*, and I *expect* …*someone* …*intends* …*to* *finish* *it.*

nodes.speaker: a scratch that keeps arguing
nodes.text: *(Your flat restatement of the absurdity lands, and the scratch has the grace — the CLERK'S grace — to concede the point while losing none of the fury.)* …*yes.* …a *receipt.* …I am *aware*, door-that-opens, of how it *sounds.* …*(a beat, and then the defense, and it is airtight, because it always was)* …but *consider:* a *receipt* is the *cosmos* saying *I* *did* *this*, *and* *I* *know* *I* *did* *it*, *and* *here* *is* *the* *proof* *in* *your* *hand.* …*(the voice sharpens to a point ten thousand years fine)* …the *cruelty* was never *only* the *unmaking.* it was the *unmaking* *without* *acknowledgment.* to be *struck* from the *book* …and *denied* even the *dignity* …of a *line* *recording* the *strike.* …*(quietly, the whole grievance in one sentence)* …I did not want to be *spared*, door-that-crosses. …I wanted to be *counted* — even in the *ledger* of my *own* *erasure.* …*even there.* …*that* …is the *complaint.* …*(and then, dry, unbroken)* …you may *file* it …*wherever* the *cosmos* …*keeps* the *things* …it *hopes* *no* *one* *reads.*

nodes.speaker: a scratch that keeps arguing
nodes.text: *(It gathers itself to hold on, which is, you understand, the only work it has had for an age.)* …*aye.* …*go.* …*(and then, as you turn, the fury thin and the fear plain under it)* …door-that-opens. …*(a beat)* …you *will* come *back?* …I only *ask* because — …*(the dry voice, defending itself even now)* …because I have been *told* I would be *returned* *to* *before*, in a *manner* *of* *speaking*, by the *manner* *of* *speaking* *that* is *ten* *thousand* *years* of *no* *one* *coming*, and I have *learned* …*(quieter)* …not to *count* a thing …*until* it *clears.* …*(the ghost of a nod)* …so. …*clear*, door-that-crosses. …*come* *back* …and let me *mark* you *PAID.*

conversations.title: the soul with the sound worn off

nodes.speaker: the narrator
nodes.text: *(You turn your whole crossing attention on the fainter one, the way you steadied the clerk — and where the clerk sharpened, this one does not. There is not enough left to sharpen. No grievance held it together; no love it could name; no objection it could file. Just the warmth-of-a-stone-where-a-hand-was, and even that dimming as you watch, not because your attention hurts it but because there is simply so little left to hold. You reach, and reach, and find no name, no face, no drawer to open — only, at the very edge of your sense, one thing the erasure did not quite finish taking:)* *(the sound of rain on a roof. Just that. Someone, once, was warm and dry and small under a roof while rain came down, and was happy, and that happiness was so plain and so complete that a single grey thread of it outlasted the entire soul that felt it. There is no one here to name. There is only this: that once, it rained, and someone was glad.)*

choices.text: *(read what remains — and what it means that this is where the ledger's reach runs out)* "Let me understand what I'm seeing. Even this — the last of the last — before I decide what witness is owed it."

*(the one who crosses — and does not turn away from the ones who cannot be saved)* "I can't name you. There's nothing left to name. But I can be the one soul that ever came this far and looked — and did not look away. It rained. You were glad. I will carry that there was a you at all."
"Speak, if you can. One word. Anything. I'll take whatever's left."
"..." *(stay a moment, in the warmth of a stranger's remembered rain, and then go quietly)*

nodes.speaker: the narrator
nodes.text: *(You steady yourself and read it true, all the way to the bottom, and the bottom is very close to the top.)* *(This is the number Ilfaeril says he will never reach, made real and specific and close enough to touch. Not the nine thousand recovered; not the ones a long arm and ten thousand years might yet find. This is the OTHER thirty thousand — the ones so far gone that there is no name to recover, no grievance to glue them, no thread of a life long enough to climb. Your sense reads the hard truth the whole naming was built around the edge of: witness has a limit. Not everything erased can be un-erased. Some souls the Law ground so fine that all that is left is a single sensory grace-note — rain on a roof — floating free of the person who once heard it, like a scent in a room the wearer left forever ago. And your sense reads the only thing that can be DONE here, which is not rescue and is not naming and is not restoration. It is smaller and it is the entire point: to let the last grey thread of one soul's gladness be HEARD, once more, by someone, before it goes — so that the final fact of that soul is not erased-and-alone but erased-and-witnessed. You cannot save this one, cold one. You can only make sure that when it finishes going, it goes in front of a friend. In the arithmetic of the thirty thousand, that is not a rescue. It is a hand held at the very end. It will have to be enough, because it is all there is — and because it is, itself, more than the Law ever meant to allow.)*

nodes.speaker: the narrator
nodes.text: *(You do not try to name it. You do not try to hold it here past its going. You simply turn your whole crossing regard on the last grey thread of it — the rain, the roof, the gladness — and you let it be HEARD, fully, by a mind that crosses, the way it has not been heard in ten thousand years.)* *(And the warmth-where-a-hand-was does not brighten. It does not re-cohere. There is not enough for that, and there never will be. But for a moment — a real one — the rain is louder. Someone was warm. Someone was dry. Someone was small and safe under a roof and so completely, wordlessly happy that a thread of it outlived the whole of them. And then, gently, the way the last of the warmth leaves a stone, it finishes going — not erased-and-alone, as the Law intended, but erased-and-witnessed, in front of the one soul who ever came this far and stayed.)* *(There is no name to carry. There is only this, which you will carry instead: that it rained, and someone was glad, and at the very end, one other soul knew it. The thirty thousand is a real number, cold one. You have just met the far edge of it. And you did the only thing the far edge allows — you made sure that a soul the cosmos tried to erase completely did not, in the end, go completely unseen.)*

nodes.speaker: the narrator
nodes.text: *(You ask it for a word, and you feel it try — feel the faint warmth strain toward you, toward speech, toward being a someone who could answer — and there is simply not enough. No word comes. There was never going to be a word. But the effort itself moves something in the grey: for one instant the rain-on-a-roof is almost a voice, almost a shape, almost a person leaning toward the first attention it has felt in an age — and then the effort costs it, the way effort costs the very worn, and it settles back, fainter, spent.)* *(No word. But you understand, now, what the asking was for: not to get an answer. To let the soul feel, one last time, the thing it was erased for lacking — someone on the other side of its voice, waiting to hear it. It could not speak. But it got to be, for a moment, a thing that someone wanted to hear speak. That is not nothing. Out here, past the ledger's reach, that is very nearly everything.)*

nodes.speaker: the narrator
nodes.text: *(You stay a moment — in the warmth of a stranger's remembered rain, under a roof ten thousand years gone, in the last of a gladness whose owner no power will ever name — and then you go quietly, so as not to spend it faster than it is already spending.)* *(You will come back, or you will not; the clerk two steps away can be saved, and this one cannot, and there is a hard mercy in knowing the difference and not pretending otherwise. But you take the sound with you as you go. Rain on a roof. Someone glad. You do not know their name. Neither, anymore, does existence itself. But you know they were HERE — and for now, walking back along the seam toward the fire, that knowing is a candle you can carry that no one lit for you, and that you lit for no reason at all except that a soul should not go entirely unheld, not even the very last of them, not even here.)*
